In order to get Full access of Marketing API Access Tier, your app needs to meet these requirements:
- Have successfully made at least 500 Marketing API calls in the last 15 days.
- Have made Marketing API calls with an error rate of less than 15% in the last 500 calls.
If you’re managing someone’s ads, use the `scope` parameter to prompt them for the `ads_management` or `ads_read` permissions. Your app gets access when they click **Allow**.
```
https://www.facebook.com/v27.0/dialog/oauth?
client_id=<YOUR_APP_ID>
&redirect_uri=<YOUR_URL>
&scope=ads_management
```
**Note:** When inputting the `YOUR_URL` field, put a trailing `/` (for example, http://www.facebook.com/).
##### Example Use Cases
| Use Case | What To Request |
|---|---|
| You want to read and manage ads for ad accounts you own or have been granted access to by the ad account owner. | - **Permission:** `ads_management` - **Feature:** Marketing API Access Tier |
| You want to read ad reports for ad accounts you own or have been granted access to by the ad account owner. | - **Permission:** `ads_read` - **Feature:** Marketing API Access Tier |
| You want to pull ad reports from a set of clients and to both read and manage ads from another set of clients. | - **Permissions:** `ads_management` and `ads_read` - **Feature:** Marketing API Access Tier |

title: Meta (Facebook) ads API explained: access, keys and cost
snippet:
The Meta Marketing API is how software creates, changes and reports on Facebook and Instagram ads — the same things you do in Ads Manager, through code. There is no “API key”: you create an app at developers.facebook.com, get an app ID and secret, and make calls with an access token. Meta charges nothing for the calls; for your own ad account an app with basic access is enough, while managing other people’s accounts needs app review and business verification. If you don’t want to write code, you don’t need your own app at all: Meta’s official MCP connector or a third-party one lets ChatGPT or Claude use the API for you.

title: Brand safety and suitability partner setup
snippet:
**Warning:** **Ads Management Standard Access is now Marketing API Access Tier**
**No code changes are needed.**
Tier labels have been updated: "Standard Access" is now **Limited Access**, and "Advanced Access" is now **Full Access**. The revised qualification threshold for Full Access has been reduced from 1,500 to **500 Marketing API calls** in the past 15 days. The underlying permission identifier remains the same, and existing access levels are preserved automatically. Learn more in the [Marketing API Access Tier documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/features-reference#marketing-api-access-tier).

To leverage Meta's Marketing API (required for program participation), you need to set up a [Meta Developer account](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/development) and [create a Meta App](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/development/create-an-app).
### Create an app
1. Go to [developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com).
2. Log in with your personal Facebook account. (This step should enable Developer access for your Facebook account.)
3. Once logged in, select My Apps and click on Create App.
4. In the subsequent screen, ensure that the App is linked to your Business; choose a relevant name and contact email, and describe the purpose of the App, before clicking Create.

You need to obtain access to the relevant Ad Accounts your client wants included for Brand Safety and Suitability. This is achieved by your client, and their third-parties, sharing all relevant Ad Accounts to your Meta Business Suite. Ask the client to go to the Ad Account in their own Business Settings and click Assign Partner. Provide them with your Business ID and ask for View Performance access, so that they can complete the Assign Partner flow. See [Add ad accounts in Meta Business Suite](https://business.facebook.com/business/help/915885887059947?id=420299598837059). At this point, the Client Ad Account should be visible in Business Settings.

title: Permissions Reference for Meta Technologies APIs
snippet:
Permissions are a form of granular, app user-granted Graph API authorization. Before your app can use an API endpoint to access your app user’s data, your app user must grant your app all permissions required by that endpoint.
**Only select permissions that your app needs to function as intended. Selecting unneeded permissions is a common reason for rejection during app review.**

### Requirements
- [Meta App Review](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/app-review) – For apps that needs access to data that you do not own or manage
- [Business Verification](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/development/release/business-verification) – is required for all apps making requests for [Advanced Access](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview/access-levels#advanced-access)
- If your app requests permission to use an endpoint to access an app user’s data, you may need to complete [data handling questions](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/development/release/data-handling-questions/questions-preview).
- You may also be required to complete an annual [Data Use Checkup](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/resp-plat-initiatives/individual-processes/data-use-checkup).

title: Meta Ad Library API: access, cost, and what it returns
snippet:
- Meta's Ad Library API returns political and issue ads worldwide and any ad shown in the UK or EU. A US-only commercial ad is not in it.
- Meta lists no fee. Access takes three steps: confirm your identity at facebook.com/ID, create a Meta for Developers account, add an app.
- For commercial ads in any country, our Meta Ads API returns the public Ad Library as JSON: 1 credit per call of up to 10 ads, 100 free credits a month.

Access takes three steps. You confirm your identity and location at facebook.com/ID, the same check required to run ads about social issues, elections or politics, which can take a few days. You create a Meta for Developers account and agree to the Platform Policy. You add an app, and every call then passes an `access_token`. You need a Facebook account for all three.
Meta lists no price or paid tier, so what it costs you is the setup and the coverage limit. The reference documents a rate-limit error, code 613, but no number for the limit.

ToolzerHub's Meta Ads API returns up to 10 ads per call, Meta's own page size, and each call costs 1 credit. 1,000 ads are 100 credits: free inside the 100 credits every account gets each month, or about $0.19 from a $19 pack of 10,000 credits that never expire. Checking 30 competitors once a day is about 900 calls a month, one call each, which is enough while a brand adds 10 or fewer ads a day. That fits one pack many times over, and [plans](https://toolzerhub.com/pricing) cover tracking that never stops.

title: Meta Ads API: Access, Tokens, Objects, First Call
snippet:
The Meta Ads API is Meta's Marketing API, the part of the Graph API at graph.facebook.com that creates and reads ads. To use it you need a Meta app with the Marketing API product, the ads_management permission, and Full Access in the Marketing API Access Tier for production volume. Calls need a user or system user access token and follow ad account, campaign, ad set, ad.
The Meta Ads API is Meta's **Marketing API**: the set of Graph API endpoints at `graph.facebook.com` that create, change, and report on ads across Facebook, Instagram, and Meta's other apps. Getting production access takes three things: a Meta app with the Marketing API product, the **`ads_management`** permission, and **Full Access** in what Meta now calls the **Marketing API Access Tier**.

1. **Create a Meta app** of the Business type in the [App Dashboard](https://developers.facebook.com/apps/) and add the Marketing API product.
2. **Request `ads_management`** (and `ads_read` if you only report). Meta's [permissions reference](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/permissions) says `ads_management` "allows your app to both read and manage the Ads account it owns" or one its owner grants you.
3. **Get Advanced Access to the permission** if you manage other people's ad accounts. Meta's [access levels page](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview/access-levels) says Standard Access permissions "can only be requested from app users who have a role on the requesting app," and that "Business Verification is required to get Advanced Access."
4. **Upgrade the Marketing API Access Tier** from Limited Access to Full Access through App Review.
5. **Have the person who authorizes hold a role on the ad account.** A token can only reach ad accounts its owner can reach.

Here is what each tier gets you, per Meta's authorization and [rate limiting](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/overview/rate-limiting) docs:
| | **Limited Access** (default) | **Full Access** (App Review) |
|---|---|---|
| Intended for | Development only | Production apps for live advertisers |
| Ads management quota per ad account per hour | 300 + 40 × active ads | 100,000 + 40 × active ads |
| System users per business | 1, plus 1 admin system user | 10, plus 1 admin system user |
| To qualify | Automatic | 500+ Marketing API calls in 15 days, error rate under 15% on the last 500 |
